answers.label: Q.1
answers.solution:
Take away each remainder from its number. The required number divides the results exactly.
\(398 - 7 = 391\), \(436 - 11 = 425\), \(542 - 15 = 527\)
Factorise: \(391 = 17 \times 23\), \(425 = 17 \times 25 = 5^2 \times 17\), \(527 = 17 \times 31\)
The only common factor is 17, so HCF \((391, 425, 527) = 17\).
Check: 17 is larger than every remainder (7, 11, 15), so the remainders are possible.
So, the largest number is 17.

answers.label: Q.3
answers.solution:
Perimeter of a rectangle \(= 2 \times (\text{length} + \text{breadth})\)
Length + breadth \(= (-6p^3 + 7p^2q^2 + pq) + (-5p^3 + 9p^2q^2 + 7pq)\)
\(= (-6 - 5)p^3 + (7 + 9)p^2q^2 + (1 + 7)pq = -11p^3 + 16p^2q^2 + 8pq\)
Perimeter \(= 2(-11p^3 + 16p^2q^2 + 8pq) = -22p^3 + 32p^2q^2 + 16pq\)
So, the perimeter is \(-22p^3 + 32p^2q^2 + 16pq\).

answers.label: Q.4
answers.solution:
Numerator: \(a^{-17} \times (a^4)^8 \times (8a^3)^{\frac{2}{3}} = a^{-17} \times a^{32} \times 8^{\frac{2}{3}} a^{2}\)
\(8^{\frac{2}{3}} = (2^3)^{\frac{2}{3}} = 2^2 = 4\), so the numerator \(= 4a^{-17 + 32 + 2} = 4a^{17}\)
Denominator: \((16a^4)^{\frac{1}{4}} \times (a^2)^8 = 16^{\frac{1}{4}} a \times a^{16}\)
\(16^{\frac{1}{4}} = (2^4)^{\frac{1}{4}} = 2\), so the denominator \(= 2a^{17}\)
LHS \(= \frac{4a^{17}}{2a^{17}} = 2 =\) RHS.
So, the expression equals 2. Hence shown.

answers.label: Q.5
answers.finalAnswer: Regular pentagon: interior angle 108° = 3 × 36° (exterior angle of a regular decagon)
answers.solution:
The printed question does not name the polygon; the statement is true for a regular pentagon, which is the polygon meant.
Exterior angle of a regular decagon (10 sides) \(= \frac{360^\circ}{10} = 36^\circ\)
Three times this angle \(= 3 \times 36^\circ = 108^\circ\)
Exterior angle of a regular pentagon (5 sides) \(= \frac{360^\circ}{5} = 72^\circ\)
Interior angle of a regular pentagon \(= 180^\circ - 72^\circ = 108^\circ\)
(or \(\frac{(5 - 2) \times 180^\circ}{5} = 108^\circ\))
So, the interior angle of a regular pentagon \(= 108^\circ = 3 \times 36^\circ\), three times the exterior angle of a regular decagon. Hence proved.

answers.label: Q.6
answers.solution:
Let the old price be Rs 100 per kg and the old consumption 1 kg, so the expenditure is Rs 100.
New price \(= 100 + 20\% \text{ of } 100 = \text{Rs } 120\) per kg.
For the expenditure to stay Rs 100, the new consumption \(= \frac{100}{120} = \frac{5}{6}\) kg.
Reduction \(= 1 - \frac{5}{6} = \frac{1}{6}\) kg.
Percentage reduction \(= \frac{1}{6} \times 100\% = 16\frac{2}{3}\%\)
(Shortcut: \(\frac{20}{100 + 20} \times 100\% = 16\frac{2}{3}\%\).)
So, Dinesh should reduce his consumption by \(16\frac{2}{3}\%\).

answers.label: Q.7
answers.solution:
Let the HCF be \(h\). Then the LCM \(= 9h\).
HCF + LCM \(= h + 9h = 10h = 500\)
\(h = \frac{500}{10} = 50\)
(Then LCM \(= 450\), and \(50 + 450 = 500\).)
So, the HCF is 50.

answers.label: Q.9
answers.solution:
Let the money he had at first be Rs \(x\).
After losing 20%, he has \(\frac{80}{100}x = \frac{4}{5}x\).
He spends 25% of this, so he keeps 75% of it: \(\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{4}{5}x = \frac{3}{5}x\)
\(\frac{3}{5}x = 480\)
\(x = \frac{480 \times 5}{3} = 800\)
So, he originally had Rs 800.

answers.label: Q.11
answers.solution:
The cars move towards each other and are still 30 km apart after 6 hours (they have not yet met).
Distance covered together in 6 hours \(= 690 - 30 = 660\) km
Sum of their speeds \(= \frac{660}{6} = 110\) km/h
Let the faster car's speed be \(x\) km/h; the slower car's speed is \((x - 10)\) km/h.
\(x + (x - 10) = 110\), so \(2x = 120\), \(x = 60\)
Slower car \(= 60 - 10 = 50\) km/h.
(If instead the cars had crossed and were 30 km apart after passing, the sum of speeds would be \(\frac{720}{6} = 120\) km/h, giving 65 km/h and 55 km/h; the usual reading is that they have not yet met.)
So, the speeds are 60 km/h and 50 km/h.

answers.label: Q.12
answers.solution:
Volume of brass \(= 2.2\) cubic dm \(= 2.2 \times 1000 = 2200\ \text{cm}^3\) (since \(1\ \text{dm}^3 = 1000\ \text{cm}^3\))
Radius of the wire \(= \frac{0.50}{2} = 0.25\) cm \(= \frac{1}{4}\) cm
Volume of the wire \(= \pi r^2 h = \frac{22}{7} \times \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{4} \times h\)
\(\frac{22}{7} \times \frac{1}{16} \times h = 2200\)
\(h = \frac{2200 \times 7 \times 16}{22} = 100 \times 7 \times 16 = 11200\) cm
\(11200\) cm \(= 112\) m
So, the length of the wire is 112 m.

answers.label: Q.13
answers.solution:
Let the three consecutive numbers be \(x - 1\), \(x\), \(x + 1\).
\((x - 1) + x + (x + 1) = 156\)
\(3x = 156\), so \(x = 52\)
The numbers are 51, 52 and 53.
\(52 = 13 \times 4\), while 51 and 53 are not multiples of 13.
So, the number which is a multiple of 13 is 52.

answers.label: Q.14
answers.solution:
Note: as printed with a plus sign, neither number is a perfect cube, and the sum does not simplify to a whole number: \(\sqrt[3]{968} + \sqrt[3]{1375} = 2\sqrt[3]{121} + 5\sqrt[3]{11} \approx 21.01\). The numbers are chosen so that their PRODUCT is a perfect cube, so the sign is meant to be \(\times\).
Prime factors: \(968 = 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 11 \times 11 = 2^3 \times 11^2\)
\(1375 = 5 \times 5 \times 5 \times 11 = 5^3 \times 11\)
\(\sqrt[3]{968} \times \sqrt[3]{1375} = \sqrt[3]{968 \times 1375} = \sqrt[3]{2^3 \times 5^3 \times 11^3}\)
\(= 2 \times 5 \times 11 = 110\)
So, the answer is 110.

answers.label: Q.17
answers.finalAnswer: 100 tickets of Rs 2.50; 200 tickets of Rs 5
answers.solution:
Let \(x\) tickets of Rs 2.50 and \(y\) tickets of Rs 5 be sold.
\(x + y = 300\) ... (1)
\(2.5x + 5y = 1250\); multiply by 0.4: \(x + 2y = 500\) ... (2)
Subtract (1) from (2): \(y = 200\)
From (1): \(x = 300 - 200 = 100\)
Check: \(100 \times 2.50 + 200 \times 5 = 250 + 1000 = 1250\).
So, 100 tickets of Rs 2.50 and 200 tickets of Rs 5 were sold.

answers.label: Q.18
answers.solution:
Outcomes when a die is tossed once: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. Total outcomes \(= 6\).
(a) Even prime numbers among them: only 2. Favourable outcomes \(= 1\).
P(even prime) \(= \frac{1}{6}\)
(b) A number that is neither prime nor composite: only 1 (2, 3, 5 are prime; 4, 6 are composite). Favourable outcomes \(= 1\).
P(neither prime nor composite) \(= \frac{1}{6}\)
So, (a) \(\frac{1}{6}\); (b) \(\frac{1}{6}\).

answers.label: Q.19
answers.solution:
Length of strip \(= 8\frac{3}{4} = \frac{35}{4}\) cm, width \(= 1\frac{1}{4} = \frac{5}{4}\) cm, diameter of each circle \(= \frac{5}{4}\) cm.
The width equals the diameter, so the circles fit in one row.
Number of circles \(= \frac{35}{4} \div \frac{5}{4} = 7\)
Area of the strip \(= \frac{35}{4} \times \frac{5}{4} = \frac{175}{16}\ \text{cm}^2\)
Radius of a circle \(= \frac{5}{8}\) cm. Area of one circle \(= \frac{22}{7} \times \frac{5}{8} \times \frac{5}{8} = \frac{275}{224}\ \text{cm}^2\)
Area of 7 circles \(= 7 \times \frac{275}{224} = \frac{275}{32}\ \text{cm}^2\)
Wastage \(= \frac{175}{16} - \frac{275}{32} = \frac{350 - 275}{32} = \frac{75}{32}\ \text{cm}^2 = 2\frac{11}{32}\ \text{cm}^2\) (about 2.34 cm²)
So, Shalini can cut 7 full circles, and the wastage is \(\frac{75}{32}\ \text{cm}^2\).

answers.solution:
In rectangle PQRS the diagonals PR and SQ are equal and bisect each other at O, so \(OP = OQ\).
In \(\triangle OPQ\), \(OP = OQ\), so \(\angle OQP = \angle OPQ = 48^\circ\), i.e. \(\angle SQP = 48^\circ\).
SR \(\parallel\) PQ and SQ is a transversal, so \(\angle RSQ = \angle SQP\) (alternate angles).
So, \(\angle RSQ = 48^\circ\).

answers.label: Q.21
answers.solution:
Take the LCM of 9 and 11, which is 99, as the number of toffees in each lot.
Cost of 99 toffees at 9 for Rs 10 \(= \frac{10}{9} \times 99 = \text{Rs } 110\)
Cost of 99 toffees at 11 for Rs 10 \(= \frac{10}{11} \times 99 = \text{Rs } 90\)
Total cost price of 198 toffees \(= 110 + 90 = \text{Rs } 200\)
Selling price at 10 for Rs 10 (Re 1 each) \(= 198 \times 1 = \text{Rs } 198\)
SP is less than CP, so there is a loss \(= 200 - 198 = \text{Rs } 2\)
Loss % \(= \frac{2}{200} \times 100 = 1\%\)
So, there is a loss of 1%.

answers.label: Q.22
answers.solution:
Radius of the pencil \(= \frac{7}{2}\) mm \(= 0.35\) cm; radius of the graphite \(= \frac{1}{2}\) mm \(= 0.05\) cm; length \(= 10\) cm.
Volume of the whole pencil \(= \pi r^2 h = \frac{22}{7} \times 0.35 \times 0.35 \times 10 = 3.85\ \text{cm}^3\)
Volume of the graphite \(= \frac{22}{7} \times 0.05 \times 0.05 \times 10 = \frac{11}{140}\ \text{cm}^3\) (about 0.0786 cm³)
Volume of the wood \(= 3.85 - \frac{11}{140} = \frac{539 - 11}{140} = \frac{528}{140} = \frac{132}{35}\ \text{cm}^3\) (about 3.771 cm³)
Weight of the wood \(= \frac{132}{35} \times 0.7 = 2.64\) g
Weight of the graphite \(= \frac{11}{140} \times 2.1 = 0.165\) g
Total weight \(= 2.64 + 0.165 = 2.805\) g
So, the pencil weighs 2.805 g.

answers.label: Q.23
answers.solution:
Let the sum be Rs \(P\).
SI for 2 years \(= \frac{P \times 10 \times 2}{100} = \frac{P}{5}\)
Amount with CI \(= P\left(1 + \frac{10}{100}\right)^2 = \frac{121}{100}P\), so CI \(= \frac{121}{100}P - P = \frac{21}{100}P\)
CI \(-\) SI \(= \frac{21}{100}P - \frac{20}{100}P = \frac{P}{100}\)
\(\frac{P}{100} = 500\), so \(P = 50000\)
So, the sum is Rs 50,000.

answers.label: Q.24
answers.solution:
The food lasts 120 men for 200 days.
After 5 days, the food left would last 120 men for \(200 - 5 = 195\) days.
Men remaining \(= 120 - 30 = 90\)
Fewer men make the food last longer (inverse proportion):
\(120 \times 195 = 90 \times d\)
\(d = \frac{120 \times 195}{90} = \frac{23400}{90} = 260\)
So, the remaining food will last 260 days.

answers.label: Q.26
answers.solution:
Old price of a bicycle \(= \text{Rs } 800\) (so at first he could buy \(\frac{20000}{800} = 25\)).
Increase \(= 25\% \text{ of } 800 = \frac{25}{100} \times 800 = \text{Rs } 200\)
New price \(= 800 + 200 = \text{Rs } 1000\)
Number he can buy now \(= \frac{20000}{1000} = 20\)
So, he can purchase 20 bicycles.

answers.label: Q.27
answers.finalAnswer: Trapezium PQRS: PQ = 8 cm, angle Q = 60°, QR = 6 cm, RS = 4 cm parallel to PQ; check angle R = 120°, PS ≈ 5.3 cm
answers.solution:
Rough sketch first: PQ is the longer parallel side at the bottom, RS (4 cm) is the shorter parallel side at the top, with R above Q's side and S above P's side.
Since PQ \(\parallel\) RS, \(\angle Q + \angle R = 180^\circ\), so \(\angle QRS = 120^\circ\).
Steps of construction:
1. Draw the line segment PQ = 8 cm.
2. At Q, construct \(\angle PQX = 60^\circ\) with compasses (an arc from Q cutting QP, then the same radius from that point).
3. With centre Q and radius 6 cm, cut QX at R. So QR = 6 cm.
4. At R, construct \(\angle QRY = 120^\circ\) on the side towards P (two 60° steps), so that RY \(\parallel\) PQ (co-interior angles add up to \(180^\circ\)).
5. With centre R and radius 4 cm, cut RY at S. So RS = 4 cm.
6. Join PS. PQRS is the required trapezium.
Measurements to check: \(\angle R = 120^\circ\); height of the trapezium \(= 6 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \approx 5.2\) cm; PS \(\approx 5.3\) cm; \(\angle P \approx 79^\circ\), \(\angle S \approx 101^\circ\); diagonal PR \(\approx 7.2\) cm, QS \(\approx 8.7\) cm.
So, PQRS is the required trapezium with PQ \(\parallel\) RS.

answers.label: Q.28
answers.finalAnswer: QR = QT; RT bisects angle R; angle STR = 90° (all proved)
answers.solution:
In the figure: \(\angle 1 = \angle PST\), \(\angle 2 = \angle TSR\), \(\angle 3 = \angle STP\), \(\angle 4 = \angle RTQ\), \(\angle 5 = \angle TRQ\), \(\angle 6 = \angle SRT\), \(\angle 7 = \angle STR\).
(a) ST bisects \(\angle S\), so \(\angle 1 = \angle 2\).
SR \(\parallel\) PQ and ST is a transversal, so \(\angle 2 = \angle 3\) (alternate angles).
Hence \(\angle 1 = \angle 3\), so in \(\triangle PST\), PT = PS (sides opposite equal angles).
PS = QR (opposite sides of a parallelogram) and PT = QT (T is the midpoint of PQ).
So QR = PS = PT = QT, i.e. QR = QT.
(b) In \(\triangle QTR\), QR = QT, so \(\angle 4 = \angle 5\) (angles opposite equal sides).
SR \(\parallel\) PQ and RT is a transversal, so \(\angle 6 = \angle 4\) (alternate angles).
Hence \(\angle 5 = \angle 6\), so RT bisects \(\angle R\).
(c) \(\angle S + \angle R = 180^\circ\) (adjacent angles of a parallelogram).
\(\angle 2 = \frac{1}{2}\angle S\) and \(\angle 6 = \frac{1}{2}\angle R\), so \(\angle 2 + \angle 6 = \frac{1}{2} \times 180^\circ = 90^\circ\).
In \(\triangle STR\), \(\angle 7 = 180^\circ - (\angle 2 + \angle 6) = 180^\circ - 90^\circ = 90^\circ\).
So, QR = QT, RT bisects \(\angle R\), and \(\angle STR = 90^\circ\). Hence proved.

answers.label: Q.29
answers.solution:
Each stack must hold books of one subject only, and every stack must hold the same number of books (same height). For the fewest stacks, the number of books in each stack is the HCF of 336, 240 and 96.
\(336 = 2^4 \times 3 \times 7\), \(240 = 2^4 \times 3 \times 5\), \(96 = 2^5 \times 3\)
HCF \(= 2^4 \times 3 = 48\)
English stacks \(= \frac{336}{48} = 7\), Mathematics stacks \(= \frac{240}{48} = 5\), Science stacks \(= \frac{96}{48} = 2\)
Total stacks \(= 7 + 5 + 2 = 14\)
So, there will be 14 stacks (48 books in each).

answers.label: Q.30
answers.solution:
When two dice are thrown, the total number of outcomes \(= 6 \times 6 = 36\).
Outcomes with a sum of 5: (1, 4), (2, 3), (3, 2), (4, 1). Favourable outcomes \(= 4\).
P(sum of 5) \(= \frac{4}{36} = \frac{1}{9}\)
So, the probability is \(\frac{1}{9}\).
